title: Comfort in Trials - Episode 3: Strength Made Perfect in Weakness

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome back to Comfort in Trials. <short pause> David here... <short pause> and I'm glad you found your way back for episode three. <chuckle> It's called Strength Made Perfect in Weakness. <short pause> Tonight, we're asking a hard question... <short pause> what do you do, when God says no?

Not the silence that might mean wait... but the clear answer that means, this thorn is staying. <short pause> Paul knew that answer. <short pause> He had seen the third heaven... received revelations beyond what words could tell. <short pause> And then came the thorn in the flesh.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: We don't know what it was. <short pause> Paul calls it a messenger of Satan, sent to buffet him. <short pause> Some trial, some weakness, some persistent pain that wouldn't go away. <short pause> Listen to what he tells the Corinthians.

And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. <short pause> For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. <short pause> And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. <short pause> Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Three times Paul asked the Lord to take it away. <short pause> Three times he prayed... and three times, the answer was no. <short pause> But notice what came with that no. <short pause> Not just refusal... but a reason. <short pause> Not just denial... but a different gift.
My grace is sufficient for thee.

Sufficient doesn't mean barely enough. <short pause> It means fully adequate. Completely supplied. All you need. <short pause> The grace was already there... present tense... enough for this very moment.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: And then the reason... for my strength is made perfect in weakness. <short pause> This is one of the strange mathematics of the kingdom. <short pause> God's strength doesn't just show up alongside our weakness. <short pause> It is made perfect... brought to completion... in the very place where we are weak.

Paul's response is remarkable. <short pause> He doesn't grit his teeth and endure. <short pause> He doesn't resign himself to fate. <short pause> He says... most gladly will I rather glory in my infirmities.

To glory means to take pleasure in... to speak openly about. <short pause> Not the thorn itself... but what the thorn makes room for. <short pause> That the power of Christ may rest upon me. <short pause> The word rest there means to spread a tent over. To dwell. <short pause> Christ's power doesn't visit. <short pause> It takes up residence in the weak place.
So Paul draws a conclusion that sounds backwards to everything the world teaches.
Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.
When I am weak, then am I strong. <short pause> Not weak and strong at the same time, as if they balance out. <short pause> But weak in himself... therefore strong in Christ.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Maybe tonight, you're living with a thorn. <short pause> Something you've prayed about. Something that limits you. Something that won't go away. <short pause> A body that doesn't work the way you need it to. <short pause> A circumstance that won't change. <short pause> A loss that has left a permanent empty place.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: The world tells you to be strong... to overcome... to push through. <short pause> But tonight, in the quiet, you can hear a different word.

My grace is sufficient. <short pause> Not someday. <short pause> Not when you're stronger. <short pause> Right now... for this thorn... for this night... for this exact measure of weakness you're carrying.

Sufficient grace means you don't have to manufacture strength you don't have. <short pause> You don't have to pretend you're fine when you're not. <short pause> You don't have to wait until you've pulled yourself together... to come to God.
The weak place. The thorn that stays. The thing you cannot fix. <short pause> That is where his power can dwell.

Paul learned to glory in his infirmities... not because he loved suffering, but because he had discovered something in it. <short pause> He had found Christ's presence in the place of weakness... and that presence was enough.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: The thorn that God allows to remain... is not a sign that he doesn't care. <short pause> It's the place he has chosen to make his strength perfect... to let his grace prove sufficient... to spread his power like a tent over you. <short pause> You don't have to be glad about the thorn itself. <short pause> But you can rest in this. <exhales> His grace is enough for it. <short pause> His power is made perfect in it. <short pause> And that is enough for tonight.

Let's pray. <short pause> Father, we bring you our thorns... the things that won't change... the weakness we carry. <short pause> Teach us that your grace is sufficient... that your strength is made perfect right here, in this.
Rest well in his sufficient grace. <short pause> Goodnight.
